text:
Nicolas Roy is a 6-foot-4 center who does the dull things well, and for a few weeks he's also been part of a line people are talking about. The Denver Post wrote on Nov. 11 that his trio with Nazem Kadri and Gabriel Landeskog found "proof of concept" in Toronto. The numbers agree so far: with Roy on the ice at five on five, Colorado takes almost 60% of shot attempts and about 56% of expected goals, nearly four points better than without him.

He has 3 goals and 7 points in 15 games on about 12 minutes a night. His chances per minute are well above last season's, the part worth watching. His wins added rank is near the bottom of the league, but that measures goals at big moments, and one of his three was an empty-netter in Montreal.

A 2023 Cup winner in Vegas and a fourth-round pick who made the long road work, Roy breaks the puck out cleanly (60% of exits with possession last season, by Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking). For a team with stars up top, a middle-six center who drives play is a real asset.
